name: Iran nuclear programme
value: No IAEA access to bombed sites; ~440 kg at 60%
summary: Iran told the IAEA it is not obliged to allow full inspections under strike threats; ~440 kg of 60% uranium unverified
state: Iran told the IAEA in a report reported on 9 Nov that it does not regard itself as obliged to allow full inspections while facing military threats (Bloomberg). On 10 Nov its foreign ministry said Iran remains in the NPT while restricting IAEA cooperation, as hardliners raise withdrawal and only Bushehr remains open to inspectors (Al Jazeera). The IAEA cannot verify about 440 kg of 60% uranium. No strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or evidence of weaponisation was found as of 11 Nov.
for_you: Curtailed inspections and US strike threats keep the risk of renewed military action in the Gulf elevated. Travellers can follow FCDO travel advice for Iran and the wider region.
rubric_hit: Inspector access curtailed and credible strike threats = Watch; no strike on nuclear sites or NPT withdrawal

sources.title: Bloomberg — Iran Hardens Line Against Nuclear Monitoring in Report to IAEA
Al Jazeera — Iran backs nuclear treaty even as hardliners raise prospect of bomb

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
